# 0010: Scenes and placeholder assets are generated by editor scripts

**Status: Accepted** (recorded from current practice in the code; not yet reviewed by the owner).

**Context.** Hand-editing Unity YAML is error-prone for agents working in parallel worktrees, and merge
conflicts in `.unity` files are hard to resolve. Scene wiring (serialized references) and placeholder
visuals must be reproducible from one command.

**Decision.** Scenes and generated assets are written by menu-driven editor scripts, not by hand:
`GameSceneGenerator` rebuilds `Assets/Scenes/Game.unity` from an empty scene, `PlaceholderVisualGenerator`
writes the placeholder `VisualDefinition` assets and `VisualRegistry`, and `MapBaker` and `TestTerrainGenerator`
write the map assets. `SceneYamlNormalizer` gives scene objects stable fileIDs so a rerun gives the same file.
`AgentFriendlyProjectSettings` forces text serialization and visible .meta files when the Editor opens.

**Consequences.** Regenerating a scene is a menu step (`LordsLegacy/Scenes/Generate Game scene`), and the
PlayMode test `GameSceneHasEveryM1PieceWired` checks the result. A hand change to the scene is lost on the next
regeneration, so edit the generator instead. Generators must be idempotent. The menu step needs the Editor, so
this is editor-lane work (decision 0007).
